Morbstack host Docker CLI plugin provenance
=============================================

Two client-side CLI plugin binaries live here. Both are host Mac (arm64)
binaries that never enter the VM/initramfs — they run directly under the
user's own `docker` CLI, which resolves subcommands like `docker compose`
and `docker buildx` via its cli-plugins mechanism
(~/.docker/cli-plugins/).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
docker-compose
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

File: docker-compose
Source: https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/download/v5.3.1/docker-compose-darwin-aarch64
Release: docker/compose v5.3.1 (latest release at time of fetch)
Platform: darwin-aarch64 (host Mac, arm64)
sha256: 32691ba1196d819fa68cbdc0aad9a5569e730a35ae40c6fdd8458110ecd69488

Verification: sha256 fetched from GitHub Release's own per-asset sidecar
file (docker-compose-darwin-aarch64.sha256, published alongside the
binary in the same release) and matched the locally computed hash
exactly.

`file` confirms: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64. Runs standalone
(`./docker-compose version` -> "Docker Compose version v5.3.1") on this
host without needing `docker` on PATH first.

Purpose: gate G4 (`docker compose up -d` via the standard compose CLI
plugin) needs the `docker compose` subcommand, which the docker CLI
resolves via its cli-plugins mechanism.

Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--compose-only).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
docker-buildx
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

File: docker-buildx
Source: https://github.com/docker/buildx/releases/download/v0.36.0/buildx-v0.36.0.darwin-arm64
Release: docker/buildx v0.36.0 (latest release at time of fetch)
Platform: darwin-arm64 (host Mac, arm64)
sha256: 82c6a3d9df37790c5bdb0d7ca88986d1d17622fc2b88ebe34b275c6c47acd7a6

Verification: docker/buildx's release does NOT put darwin hashes in its
plain `checksums.txt` asset (that file only lists linux/freebsd/netbsd/
openbsd builds) — the darwin (and windows) hashes live in the separate
`checksums-signed.txt` asset for the same release instead. The pin above
was matched against that file's
"82c6a3d9...  *buildx-v0.36.0.darwin-arm64" line, and independently
cross-checked against the GitHub Releases API's own per-asset "digest"
field for that same asset (`GET /repos/docker/buildx/releases/latest`,
`assets[].digest` = "sha256:82c6a3d9..."), which agreed exactly. Both
matched the locally computed hash of the downloaded file.

`file` confirms: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64. Runs standalone
(`./docker-buildx version` -> "github.com/docker/buildx v0.36.0 ...") on
this host without needing `docker` on PATH first.

Purpose: parity check #13/#14 in docs/parity.md — the guest's dockerd
ships upstream BuildKit and it is fully functional (multi-platform
builds, cache mounts, everything works), but no `docker-buildx` client
binary was shipped anywhere in the repo, so `docker build` (BuildKit is
the default builder since Docker 23+) and `docker buildx build` both
failed out of the box with a stock docker CLI: `docker: 'buildx' is not
a docker command`. This is the single highest-ROI fix identified by that
audit. Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--buildx-only).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Installing either plugin
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Neither binary is installed into ~/.docker/cli-plugins/ by the fetch
script itself — fetching is a repo-local caching step and must not touch
the user's dotfiles without being asked. Two supported ways to install:

  1. `morb install-cli-plugins` — explains exactly what it will do
     (symlink docker-compose and docker-buildx from here into
     ~/.docker/cli-plugins/), asks for confirmation, and does nothing
     without an explicit yes (or `--force`). See `morb install-cli-plugins
     --print-plan` to see the plan without being prompted, and `morb
     install-cli-plugins --json` for scriptable output.

  2. The manual one-liner, if you would rather do it yourself:
       mkdir -p ~/.docker/cli-plugins
       ln -sf "$(pwd)/dist/host-bin/docker-compose" ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose
       ln -sf "$(pwd)/dist/host-bin/docker-buildx" ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx
